## Intent
Hypothesis: branchy respawn forces scalar (de-vectorized) per-particle processing that cannot approach the streaming ceiling, remaining overhead-bound regardless of N.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is FLAT across N at every death rate, with no cache-spill knee. At q=0.01, cost drops slightly from 8.364 ns/p (N=4000, past the L1d spill at N≈963) to 7.811 (N=1M) — minor overhead amortization, then stable through the L2 spill at N≈61680 to N=4M (7.87). Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: q=0.05 holds ~8.53–8.88, q=0.25 at ~11.1–11.9. No knee at L2→DRAM confirms the algo is not bandwidth-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.71 GB/s at N=1M, q=0.01 — 34.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound: bandwidth is flat across N (8.13–8.71 at q=0.01), never entering a streaming regime. Death rate, not N, drives degradation: q=0.05 falls to 7.97 GB/s (31.6%), q=0.25 to 6.10 GB/s (24.2%), as branchy respawn cost rises with churn.

## Assembly
No vectorization. The sole vector-suffixed instruction is `movi.2d v10, #0` (zero-init). All FP uses scalar `s` registers: `ldr s0`, `fmul s1, s1, s8`, `fadd s0, s0, s1`. No gather — loads are scalar `ldr s`/`ldp s` from contiguous particle fields. The 19 `strb` byte stores and 12 `ldrb` byte loads implement RGBA scatter with `csel` clamping (18 instances). Heavy control flow — 21 `b`, 19 `cmp`, 4 `tbnz` — plus `udiv`/`msub` for spawn-index and 3 `bl` calls explain the scalar floor: branches and byte-granular scatter prevent streaming.

## Verdict
Holds — scalar code never exceeds 8.71 GB/s (34.5% of ceiling) at q=0.01, and the flat N-curve (7.81–8.36 ns/p) confirms overhead-bound behavior. At q=0.25, cost rises to 11.2 ns/p (6.04 GB/s, 24%) with no N-dependence, confirming branchy respawn — not memory — is the binding constraint.
